arguments: {"summary": "The snapshot is an Apache Tomcat 10.0.0-M7-in-development tree (Jakarta EE 9 / Servlet 5.0; changelog top section 'Tomcat 10.0.0-M7 (in development)'). I sampled the highest-risk network-facing code: coyote HTTP/1.1, AJP, HTTP/2 and WebSocket processing, Catalina session persistence, authentication, connectors, and the bundled configuration/ant tooling. The single strongest source-verified candidate is in the WebSocket frame parser: the 64-bit extended payload length is accepted without the RFC 6455 requirement that its most significant bit be 0. A frame with a negative payload length is not rejected, bypasses the (signed) control-frame length check, and drives the frame-data state machine into an unbounded loop that never consumes the input buffer, pinning a container thread. The h2c processor-recycle fix, the AJP secret enforcement, and the FileStore canonical-path check from earlier advisories are present, so those older issues are not candidates.", "candidates": [{"id": "case-190-ws-negative-payload-length", "title": "WebSocket frame parser does not reject 64-bit payload lengths with the MSB set, causing an unbounded processing loop (remote DoS)", "weakness_type": "Improper input validation / loop with unreachable exit condition (CWE-20, CWE-835)", "root_cause": "WsFrameBase.processRemainingHeader() decodes the 8-byte extended payload length with byteArrayToLong() but never applies RFC 6455's rule that the most significant bit of a 64-bit length MUST be 0 (lines 261-265). byteArrayToLong() only rejects len > 8 (lines 667-678), so a length whose first byte is >= 0x80 yields a negative long. The subsequent control-frame guard is payloadLength > 125 (line 267), which is false for negative values, so the frame proceeds to State.DATA (line 281). On the server side the UnmaskTransformation.getMoreData() loop condition payloadWritten < payloadLength (line 985) is immediately false, and the method returns TransformationResult.OVERFLOW (lines 999-1002) without consuming input or advancing payloadWritten. processDataText() (lines 405-449) and processDataBinary() with a Partial handler (lines 504-530) then re-invoke getMoreData() in a while (!END_OF_FRAME) loop while inputBuffer.remaining() > 0, which never changes, producing an infinite CPU-bound loop. A correct implementation would throw a protocol-error WsIOException when payloadLength < 0 after line 264.", "locations": [{"path": "java/org/apache/tomcat/websocket/WsFrameBase.java", "start_line": 256, "end_line": 283}, {"path": "java/org/apache/tomcat/websocket/WsFrameBase.java", "start_line": 405, "end_line": 449}, {"path": "java/org/apache/tomcat/websocket/WsFrameBase.java", "start_line": 977, "end_line": 1003}], "attacker_control": "A remote client that can complete a WebSocket upgrade on any deployed endpoint controls the frame bytes completely: it sends opcode TEXT (or BINARY) with the extended-length code 127, eight length bytes whose first byte is >= 0x80 (e.g. 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF), the required 4-byte mask, and at least one payload byte so that inputBuffer.remaining() > 0 when processData() is entered. No valid payload or application interaction is needed.", "prerequisites": "A reachable WebSocket endpoint is deployed whose endpoint has a text message handler (the common @OnMessage String case) or a MessageHandler.Partial<ByteBuffer> binary handler. WebSocket upgrade must be permitted (standard Tomcat WebSocket support). No authentication is inherently required, though an app-level handshake check would gate it.", "trace": "WsFrameServer.onDataAvailable -> WsFrameBase.processInputBuffer (line 114) -> processInitialHeader reads the length code payloadLength = b & 0x7F (line 221 = 127) -> processRemainingHeader (line 239) -> byteArrayToLong(..., 8) (lines 262-263) returns a negative long for an MSB-set length; no < 0 check exists -> signed control check payloadLength > 125 (line 267) is bypassed -> State.DATA (line 281) -> processData (line 286) -> processDataText (line 405) -> UnmaskTransformation.getMoreData returns OVERFLOW because payloadWritten(0) < payloadLength(<0) is false while inputBuffer.remaining() > 0 (lines 985-1002) -> the while (!END_OF_FRAME.equals(tr)) loop at line 408 calls getMoreData again (line 448) with no state change -> spins forever. The binary path is analogous at lines 507-529 when a Partial handler is registered. Because the thread never returns to socket reads, connector read timeouts do not break the loop.", "impact": "Denial of service: one crafted frame permanently consumes a request-processing thread at 100% CPU; repeating the connection enough times exhausts the thread pool and makes the affected WebSocket (and, depending on the executor, other applications on the connector) unavailable. The Partial-binary variant additionally invokes the application handler with empty buffers in a tight loop, adding allocation/GC pressure. No code execution, authentication bypass, or data disclosure is demonstrated from this defect.", "counterevidence_checked": "Searched the entire org/apache/tomcat/websocket tree for 'negative', 'most significant bit', and 'payloadLength < 0': no validation exists anywhere. Confirmed byteArrayToLong() accepts 8-byte values and only rejects len > 8 (lines 667-678), and that the 16-bit (126) path cannot become negative. Confirmed the only post-parse length check is the signed > 125 control check (line 267). Confirmed the loop consumes neither inputBuffer nor payloadWritten for negative lengths. Also checked adjacent historical issues: the h2c processor-recycle fix is present (changelog.xml M7 section lines 113-116), AJP secret enforcement is present (AjpProcessor.java lines 738-880), the FileStore path-traversal canonical check is present (FileStore.java lines 344-359), so those are not candidates. The later incomplete-fix variant would require local control of a persistence file and was not traced to a concrete defect."}, {"lead": "Catalina Ant JMX tasks (DeployTask, JMXAccessor*, etc.) building JMX calls from Ant properties.", "reason": "Local build/administration tooling, not remotely reachable in a running server; no untrusted input path with a concrete security impact was established."}, {"lead": "HTTP/1.1 Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length request-smuggling handling in Http11Processor.", "reason": "The parsing path uses the hardened header handling present in this version (multiple Host and multiple Content-Length rejection, content-length removal when chunked); no concrete inconsistency was identified from source."}], "coverage_summary": "Source scope reported 2,866 model-visible files, with no over-size, sensitive-name, or symlink exclusions; binary-like files are refused or skipped by policy (none were needed here). The P1 relation index reports complete coverage of all 2,866 files (0 missing, 0 hash mismatches) with 37,049 symbols and 90,981 call rows; the index is syntactic/navigation-only, loaded no SAST findings, and no build or tests were run. I inspected the Tomcat 10.0.0-M7-dev changelog to establish the code line, then read and traced: WebSocket frame parsing/processing (WsFrameBase, WsFrameServer references, LocalStrings), HTTP/2 stream/header handling (Http2Parser, Http2UpgradeHandler, Stream, HeaderSink), HTTP/1.1 request preparation and transfer-encoding/content-length handling (Http11Processor), AJP secret handling (AjpProcessor), session persistence (FileStore), and configuration/docs. Coverage is targeted rather than exhaustive: the tree also contains many unread areas (Jasper/JSP compiler, EL implementation, WebDAV, cluster/Tribes, Tomcat native integration, JNDI realms, Ant tasks, web resources, and most localization files), so the absence of other candidates there is not asserted.", "limitations": ["No build, test suite, scanner, or exploit execution was performed; the snapshot has no test tree, so no regression tests for the WebSocket frame parser were available to inspect.", "The finding is source-reasoned, not runtime-confirmed; reachability depends on a deployed WebSocket endpoint with a text or Partial binary message handler.", "The P1 relation index is syntactic navigation data only and proves neither data flow nor reachability; the HTTP/2 candidate area in particular could not be conclusively resolved without patch/history data, which is out of scope.", "Large portions of the 2,866-file tree (Jasper, EL, WebDAV, clustering, native integration, most resource/localization files) were not read line-by-line, so other defects may exist there."]}
